content.text: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1088
Should this PR instead be targeting the 4.6.0 branch?
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/tree/4.6.0-RC
: Yes, it should be — I'll make a new PR.
New PR targeting 4.6.0-RC:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1089
I disagree strongly with this PR. It appears to conflict directly with the LDP and HTTP specifications.
: the current HTTP spec says (
https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7232#section-3.1):

An origin server MUST use the strong comparison function when comparing entity-tags for If-Match (Section 2.3.2), since the client intends this precondition to prevent the method from being applied if there have been any changes to the representation data.
Since we cannot emit strong ETags, my reading of the chart in
https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7232#section-2.3.2
is that any strong comparison involving a weak ETag must fail.  So I believe this PR faithfully implements that.
The LDP spec says we SHOULD support If-Match.  But if the above is true, then I think we cannot.  Complying with the MUST of the HTTP spec would trump a SHOULD from the LDP spec.
I read that
entirely
differently. Perhaps we should discuss this on a Tech call. I am willing to be convinced, but as it is, I would veto the current PR.

I completely agree that some discussion would help here.  There seemed to be a good consensus on the Hydra #dev slack channel yesterday, but the specs are very slippery, and there are subtle differences between the old, current and draft specs that could use some teasing out.
I've added this ticket to tomorrow's Tech call agenda:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/2016-08-11+-+Fedora+Tech+Meeting
Because we never emit strong ETags for Containers, and strong ETags are required for updates with an If-Match header, we should never accept updates to containers with an If-Match header.
Related to FCREPO-2098.
